note: Pinned inputs, criteria and provenance for the retained test corpora.

types.index: a whole number, zero or above
types.{object: name}: the object declared under that name
types.{array: type}: a non-empty list of that type
types.{map: type}: a non-empty object whose keys are arbitrary and whose values are that type
types.{quantity: type}: value of that type, with unit, origin and -- where derived -- derivation
types.filename: A relative path inside the case directory; no absolute path, empty, dot or parent segments.

reduction.note: A justified limitation of one metric; measured values retain their units and origins.

viewport.note: THE ROOM THE DOCUMENT IS LAID OUT IN, and it is part of the declaration rather than a property of whatever window is open: every offset upstream states is measured against this origin, so a viewport read from a host would make the same document state different numbers on two machines.

limits-probe.note: A CASE WHOSE VERDICT IS THAT THIS ENGINE DECLINES ITS SUBJECT (board:1424). `declines` names what -- an extension, a feature -- and the runner requires the engine's refusal to CONTAIN that name, so the case cannot pass on a refusal about something else: a corrupt file, a missing camera or a short buffer would all refuse, and none of them is what the case is about.

script-expectation.note: THE CASE STATES WHAT IS EXPECTED OF IT, IN ITS OWN FRONTMATTER (board:1450). test262 writes a `/*--- ... ---*/` block: a case with no `negative` block passes by RUNNING TO THE END, and one with a negative block passes by being REFUSED -- with the kind of refusal it named. **The kind is required for a negative case** for the same reason `limits-probe` requires `declines`: a case that passes by refusing for the wrong reason is a green light about something else.

layout-assertions.note: THE DOCUMENT STATES WHERE ITS OWN BOXES LAND (board:1444). Upstream writes `data-expected-width`, `data-expected-height`, `data-offset-x` and `data-offset-y` on the elements it means, in CSS pixels against the viewport origin, and the verdict is every one of them exactly. IT IS THE ANCHOR THE REFTEST FAMILY CANNOT BE: a pair of renders can agree because both are empty, and an absolute offset cannot.

reftest.note: TWO DOCUMENTS THIS LIBRARY DRAWS ITSELF, COMPARED BITWISE. `match` says the pair must be identical to the byte and `mismatch` says it must differ somewhere -- and the second is why the suite is not self-consistency wearing the word correctness. There is no threshold to widen here, which is what makes this suite harder than the picture suite rather than softer.

criterion.note: THREE KINDS OF CRITERION AND THE KIND DECIDES THE INSTRUMENT (board:0085). `numeric` -- the asset states a value or a relation and the acceptance is that number on the linear tap. `self-describing` -- the asset renders checkmarks, arrows or markers whose correctness is readable FROM THE PICTURE. `stated-invariant` -- the asset states a relation between two parts of its own render. `limits-probe` -- the asset states it is not expected to render correctly everywhere and has no pass at all.

script.note: A PROGRAM AND THE FILES IT IS RUN WITH. `entry` is the case; the rest are the harness files test262 states a case needs -- `assert.js` and `sta.js` unless the case declares `raw`, plus whatever its own `includes` names. They arrive in the order they must be run in, which is the order upstream states and not an order this tree chose.

document.note: MARKUP AND THE FILES IT NAMES. `entry` is the document; the rest are what its own `<link>` and `<script>` elements reach for, resolved at the pin and fetched by digest like any other subject -- so a stylesheet that changed upstream is a refusal and not a quietly different picture.

data.note: A SUBJECT THAT IS NOT GEOMETRY. A corpus whose oracle is a table of numbers stands up no asset; the case declares the table and the scenario it feeds.

geographiclib-testdata.note: PUBLISHED TEST DATA, not a repository checkout. GeodTest is generated once and released under CC0; there is no commit to pin, so the archive's own digest IS the pin.

fetched-file.note: A file may be covered by more than one grant -- MultiUVTest carries a CC-BY licence and Khronos's non-copyrightable-logo mark -- and the licence check compares the SET declared here against the set upstream's own metadata states, so both are named or the manifest was written from memory.

licence.note: Each file declares one or more grants with their holders and source URLs.
